decision.author: ezyang
decision.body:
Review by Astra agent.

Found two remaining correctness gaps in the mutation protection and a compilation failure in the budget-zero path; details are inline. Reproduced on a locally patched PyTorch 2.14 CPU wheel with the PR partitioner source (omitting references to the unavailable, unrelated distributed wait_tensors op). The PR's added regression test passes in that environment; this was not a full source-build or test-suite run.

inline_comments.body:
[P1] Follow aliases through to reads that materialize independent values

Marking only the direct reader does not preserve the input value when that reader is a view. For a zero-initialized buffer, `cond = counts.view(16) > .5; y = torch.where(cond, x * .5, x).sum(); counts.add_(1); return y` still produces gradients of **0.5 instead of eager's 1.0** at memory budgets 0 and 0.05. At budget zero the saved view aliases the mutated buffer, so recomputing the predicate observes the updated contents. Moving the mutation outside the compiled forward also still raises the version-counter error with `ban_recompute_through_buffers=True`. Please propagate the protection through aliasing operations to the actual data reads, or otherwise save an independent snapshot.

— Astra agent
inline_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -2417,6 +2418,79 @@ def force_save_bw_mutation_src(joint_module: fx.GraphModule) -> None:
             break
 
 
+def force_save_fw_mutated_input_readers(joint_module: fx.GraphModule) -> None:
+    # Recomputing a read of an input the forward mutates is not equivalent to
+    # saving that read: the mutation lands before the backward runs, so the
+    # recompute observes the post-mutation value. That yields wrong gradients, or
+    # trips SavedVariable::unpack when the input's bumped version counter is
+    # checked. Force those reads to be saved, which also keeps the mutated input
+    # from having to stay live into the backward at all.
+    mutated_inputs: OrderedSet[fx.Node] = OrderedSet()
+    mutation_values: OrderedSet[fx.Node] = OrderedSet()
+
+    # aotdispatch tells us which inputs the forward mutates. This is the
+    # authoritative signal: it also covers configurations where the mutation is
+    # applied from runtime metadata rather than kept in-graph, in which case there
+    # is no copy_ below to find.
+    unsafe_names = OrderedSet(
+        joint_module.meta.get("aot_mutated_input_names") or []
+    )
+    # A buffer read here may be mutated by a different compiled region, or by
+    # eager code, between this forward and its backward. Neither is visible in
+    # this graph, so mutates_data above says nothing about them and the only
+    # sound option is to treat every buffer as mutable.
+    if config.ban_recompute_through_buffers:
+        unsafe_names.update(joint_module.meta.get("aot_buffer_input_names") or [])
+
+    if unsafe_names:
+        for node in joint_module.graph.find_nodes(op="placeholder"):
+            if node.name in unsafe_names:
+                mutated_inputs.add(node)
+
+    for node in reversed(joint_module.graph.nodes):
+        if node.op == "output":
+            continue
+        if node.target is not torch.ops.aten.copy_.default:
+            # Same invariant as force_save_bw_mutation_src: aotdispatch only emits
+            # copy_ at the very end of the joint graph.
+            break
+        if _has_tag_must_be_in_backward(node):
+            continue
+        dst, src = node.args[0], node.args[1]
+        if isinstance(dst, fx.Node) and dst.op == "placeholder":
+            mutated_inputs.add(dst)
+            if isinstance(src, fx.Node):
+                mutation_values.add(src)
+
+    if not mutated_inputs:
+        return
+
+    # Exempt the functionalized in-place chain itself: those nodes read the
+    # pre-mutation input only to produce its new value, and the epilogue consumes
+    # them in the forward. Walk only through nodes that themselves take a mutated
+    # input, never all transitive ancestors -- the mutation's value can depend on
+    # arbitrary earlier computation (e.g. dependent task arches feeding the update),
+    # and exempting that would skip genuine readers of the same input.
+    mutation_chain: OrderedSet[fx.Node] = OrderedSet()
+    stack = list(mutation_values)
+    while stack:
+        node = stack.pop()
+        if node in mutation_chain:
+            continue
+        if not any(inp in mutated_inputs for inp in node.all_input_nodes):
+            continue
+        mutation_chain.add(node)
+        stack.extend(node.all_input_nodes)
+
+    for node in joint_module.graph.nodes:
+        if node.op != "call_function" or node in mutation_chain:
+            continue
+        if _has_tag_must_be_in_backward(node):
+            continue
+        if any(inp in mutated_inputs for inp in node.all_input_nodes):
+            node.meta["recompute"] = CheckpointPolicy.MUST_SAVE

inline_comments.body:
[P1] Do not exempt mutation values that also feed backward computation

Being the source of the mutation epilogue does not mean this value is used only for the update. Starting from a zero buffer, `counts.add_(1); return torch.where(counts > 1.5, x * .5, x).sum()` functionalizes to an `add` feeding both the predicate and the final `copy_`. This exemption leaves the `add` recomputable, so backward adds 1 to the already-updated buffer and evaluates a different predicate. I reproduced gradients of **0.5 instead of eager's 1.0** at budgets 0 and 0.05 with `keep_inference_input_mutations=True`. Please restrict the exemption to values that cannot participate in backward recomputation, or protect the reads through this chain too.

— Astra agent

inline_comments.body:
[P2] Save tensor outputs rather than tuple-valued MUST_SAVE nodes

This list can contain tuple-producing operations newly marked by `force_save_fw_mutated_input_readers`. For example, `cond = counts.sort().values > .5; y = torch.where(cond, x * .5, x).sum(); counts.add_(1); return y` marks `aten.sort.default` MUST_SAVE. With `activation_memory_budget=0`, compilation then fails in `_categorize_saved_tensors_for_backward` with `expected one saved_tensor_is_graph_input entry per saved tensor, got 0 != 1`, because the saved value is the sort tuple rather than a tensor. The same example compiles and matches eager at budget 0.05. Please expand multi-output nodes to their tensor leaves before constructing the budget-zero saved-value set.

— Astra agent
